app.signedOut: Open this page once with {token} followed by your {env} to sign in.
app.live.title: Visitors in the last five minutes
compare.title: Compare to
calendar.pick: Pick a start and an end day
hint.visitors: Different people, counted once a day
hint.visits: A visit is a session, and it ends after 30 idle minutes
hint.bounceRate: A visit with one pageview and no event that lasts under ten seconds
hint.visitDuration: Average time per visit while the page was visible and in focus
delta.title: Against the comparison period
chart.label: {metrics} over time
chart.scaled: Each line is scaled to its own peak. Hover for values.
chart.pick: Click cards to add them to the chart.
map.label: Visitors by country: {top}
map.title: Around the world
filter.title: Show visits
filter.placeholder: Type a value or pick one below
filter.note: Every condition has to hold. Click any row on the dashboard to add one without opening this.
settings.title: Settings
settings.timezoneHint: Days in your reports start at midnight here.
install.live: Receiving visits. The last one was {when}.
install.none: No visits yet. Add the script below, then open a page on your site.
install.script: Add this to every page, just before {tag}.
install.events: Clicks on anything can be counted with no JavaScript.
install.eventsJs: You can also send events from JavaScript, for things that are not clicks.
install.agents: To see AI agents like ChatGPT and Claude reading your pages, pass each request to Runlight in your middleware with the code below.
install.ignored: Your visits from this browser are not counted.
install.counted: Your visits from this browser are counted.
install.ignoreElsewhere: Dashboard on a different domain from the site? Open {link} once in each browser you use.
links.name: Name
links.slugPlaceholder: Leave blank for a random one
links.confirmDelete: Delete {name}? Its clicks stay in your stats.
links.importHelp: Use the columns name and url, plus slug and domain when you have them.
links.domainsHelp: Use a domain or subdomain you own for short links, like t.example.com. Links on it live at its root, as in t.example.com/sale.
links.step1: At your DNS provider, add a CNAME record for the subdomain that points to {host}, where this dashboard runs. For a bare domain with no subdomain, use an A or ALIAS record to the same server instead.
links.step2: Make your host accept the domain and serve HTTPS for it. On Vercel or Netlify, add it to your project's domains, and on your own server, add it to the config and the certificate. If Runlight runs inside your app, pass requests to rl.linkDomainResponse() in your middleware.
links.step3: Add the domain below. Runlight then checks that it reaches this dashboard.
links.removeNote: Removing a domain keeps its links and their clicks. They move to {fallback} until you add the domain back, then return to it.
prompt.domainHint: Copy these steps with your addresses filled in, and paste them into it.
prompt.installHint: Copy the setup steps and paste them into it.
import.intro: Bring your short links over from another service, with their click history where the service shares it. Your key or password is used for this import only and never saved. Importing again skips links already here.
import.done: Finished: {links} links and {clicks} clicks imported, {skipped} already here.
import.stopped: Stopped after {done} of {total} links. Start again to carry on; links already imported are skipped.
import.history.full: This imports every click, with its country, device, browser, and referrer.
import.history.daily: This imports clicks per day, without country or device.
import.history.none: This imports links only, since the service does not share dated clicks.
import.umamiHelp: In Umami, create an API key under Settings, API keys. Stock self-hosted Umami has no API keys, so sign in with your username and password instead. Either one is used for this import only and never saved.
import.csvHelp: Use the columns name and url, plus slug and domain when you have them.
import.dubHelp: In Dub, create an API key under Settings, API Keys, with read access to links and analytics. Every click comes across on Business plans, daily counts on Pro, links only on Free.
import.bitlyHelp: In Bitly, go to Settings, API, enter your password, and generate a token. Bitly keeps daily counts only, as far back as your plan allows (none on Free).
import.shortioHelp: In Short.io, open Integrations and API and create a secret API key (a public key cannot read links). Short.io allows 60 statistics requests a minute, so this import paces itself.
import.rebrandlyHelp: In Rebrandly, create an API key under Settings, API keys. Rebrandly shares only total clicks, so links come across without history.
import.moveNote: Links on the service's own domain (bit.ly, dub.sh, rebrand.ly, short.gy) move to {fallback} with the same slug; branded domains are added under Custom domains.
prompt.title: Using a coding assistant?
compare.allTime: There is nothing before all time to compare with.
view.resetHint: Back to the last 30 days, with no filters or comparison
share.intro: A share link shows this site's stats to anyone who has it, with no sign-in. It never shows your short links, your settings, or the site's address.
share.namePlaceholder: Who it is for, like a client or your team
share.empty: Make one below and send it to anyone who should see these stats.
share.revokeNote: Deleting a share link stops it working at once. Anyone who had it then sees a page saying so.
share.gone: Whoever shared it has turned it off. Ask them for a new link.
live.title: Right now
live.nowHint: Anyone who viewed a page or did something in the last 5 minutes.
live.nobody: Visitors show up here as they arrive.
live.quiet: Visits from the last 30 minutes show up here.
welcome.title: Add Runlight to {name}
welcome.lead: Waiting for the first visit. This page fills in by itself once it arrives.
goals.emptyTitle: Your goals will show up here
goals.emptyHint: A goal counts what matters to you, like a signup or a click on a button. An event or page goal you add counts past visits too, and a click goal counts from when you add it.
goals.overTimeValued: Conversions and revenue over time, each on its own scale
goals.name: Name
goals.hint.event: The name you send with runlight("Name") or a data-runlight attribute.
goals.hint.page: A path like /thanks. Use * for anything: /blog/* or /thanks*. A full URL works too.
goals.hint.link: Clicks on links whose address matches. Use * for anything, like https://buy.stripe.com/*, or start with / for your own pages.
goals.hint.selector: Enter any CSS selector, or use Pick on my site, which opens your site so you can click the element and then Use this.
goals.value.prop: An amount sent with the event
goals.intro: Goals turn visits into conversions. Each one counts an event, a page visit, or a click, and can carry a money value so you can see revenue by source and page.
goals.none: Add one below to start counting it.
goals.pastNote: Goals are counted from the data you already have, so a new goal shows past conversions too. Click goals start counting within about five minutes of being added.
mail.intro: Runlight sends reports and invites through your own email service. Set it up once and every site uses it.
mail.keepSaved: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
mail.fromHint: Use an address your service lets you send from, on a domain you have verified with it.
mail.testSent: Test sent to {to}. Check the inbox, and the spam folder.
mail.notEncryptedTitle: Your keys will be stored unencrypted
mail.notEncrypted: This Runlight has no RUNLIGHT_SECRET, so the keys are kept in its database exactly as you type them. Set RUNLIGHT_SECRET or RUNLIGHT_TOKEN on the server to keep them encrypted.
reports.title: Who gets reports
reports.intro: A summary of {site} by email, with visitors, top pages, sources, countries, and conversions against the period before.
reports.none: Add an email address below to start sending them.
reports.when: Weekly reports cover Monday to Sunday and go out on Monday from 8am, monthly ones on the 1st, in this site's timezone. They are sent by the hourly check (a cron calling POST /api/check).
reports.needsMail: Reports start going out once an email service is set up. One service sends them for every site.
email.footer: You get this {frequency} report for {site} from Runlight.
email.test.subject: Runlight can send email
email.test.body: This test came through {service}. Reports for your sites will arrive the same way.
email.unsub.title: Stop the {site} reports?
email.unsub.body: {email} will get no more reports for this site.
email.unsub.done: No more reports for {site} will reach {email}.
email.unsub.gone: This link has been used already, or the report was removed.
tokens.intro: Ask your AI assistant about your stats. Make a token, then add Runlight to Claude, Cursor, or any app that connects to MCP servers. A read token never changes anything, and a manage token can change one site's settings. The same token works with the HTTP API.
tokens.namePlaceholder: What it is for, like Claude or a script
tokens.empty: Make one below to connect an AI assistant or a script.
tokens.revokeNote: Deleting a token stops it working at once.
tokens.once: Copy this token now. It is shown only once, and Runlight keeps only a fingerprint of it.
tokens.claudeCode: Claude Code takes the token with this command.
tokens.json: Cursor and other apps that take an mcpServers JSON config use this instead.
sites.domainsHint: Enter the domain the site runs on, like example.com, and separate several with commas.
sites.name: Name
sites.timezoneHint: Days are counted in {zone}, which you can change later in Settings.
sites.firstLead: Runlight counts each site you add here. Enter the site's domain, and the next screen shows the script tag to put on its pages.
sites.deleteHint: Deleting a site removes every visit, link, goal, and report recorded for it, and it cannot be undone.
install.ignoreServer: To stop counting your own visits, open {link} once in each browser you use.
visits.intro: Bring your Umami history over so your charts reach back before Runlight started counting. Only visits from before Runlight's own first one come across, so nothing is counted twice, and running it again carries on where it stopped.
visits.onlyUmami: Umami's API hands over every visit with its page, source, place, and device, which is what Runlight keeps. Plausible, Fathom, and Google Analytics only give out totals, and totals cannot be turned back into visits.
visits.noWebsites: This Umami account has no websites.
visits.running: {done} of {total} days read, {pageviews} pageviews so far
visits.done: Finished. {pageviews} pageviews and {events} events came across in {visits} visits.
visits.stopped: Stopped. Start again to carry on from the last day imported.
props.title: Properties
props.none: They appear once the event is sent with properties.
account.title: Account
account.owner: You are the owner, so you can change everything and manage people. Nobody else can remove you.
account.viewer: You are a viewer, so you can read every site's stats without changing anything.
account.nextHint: Use at least ten characters. Changing it signs out your other browsers.
people.intro: Everyone here can sign in to this server. Admins can change everything the owner can and manage people, though nobody can remove the owner. Members change the settings of every site, and viewers read every site's stats without changing anything. Invite a coworker and they choose their own password.
people.roles: Members can't manage people, set up the mail service or the assistant, or delete a site. Only the owner can hand ownership to an admin.
pluginKey.title: Key for CMS plugins
pluginKey.intro: The WordPress, Drupal, and Craft plugins use this key to report AI agents reading this site's pages. It can only report for this site and cannot read anything. Replacing it stops the old key at once.
export.title: Download everything in this view as CSV files
funnels.title: Funnels
funnels.intro: A funnel follows the steps you expect a visit to take, such as the pricing page and then signup, and shows how many visits made it through each step in order.
funnels.none: Add one below to see where people stop along the way.
funnels.name: Name
funnels.stepsHint: A page path can use * to match anything, like /blog/*. Each step has to happen after the one before it, in the same visit.
sites.connectIntro: Connect a site here when it already counts itself with Runlight inside its own app. Its numbers stay there. You sign in to it once and allow this server, and then you can see and change the site from here.
sites.connectTokenHint: Make a token on that install, in Settings, API and AI. With a read token the numbers show here and the settings stay there.
sites.remoteNote: This site is counted by its own Runlight at {url}, which lets this server read it. Allow changes to manage its settings from here too.
sites.disconnectHint: Disconnecting removes the site from this server. Its own Runlight and everything it has counted stay as they are.
data.retentionHint: Older visits and events are deleted for good when you save, then every day after. Goals, links, and settings stay.
data.deletesBefore: Visits before {date} will be deleted when you save.
data.unreachable: Could not reach {url} to read this setting. Try again in a minute.
data.exportHint: The ZIP holds every report for this site since its first visit, as CSV files.
sites.remoteManaged: This site is counted by its own Runlight at {url}. Changes you make here are saved there.
sites.reconnectHint: Use this if the install no longer accepts this server, for example after its token was deleted there.
sites.connectError.expired: That connection took too long or was already used. Start again.
sites.connectError.refused: The install would not let this server connect. Start again, or connect it with an API token.
sites.connectError.token: The install did not give this server a token. Start again.
sites.connectError.failed: Connecting did not finish. Start again.
mail.noneRemote: {host} has no mail service yet, so it cannot send these reports. Set one up in its own dashboard, under Settings, Email service.
account.mismatch: The two new passwords are not the same.
mail.introRemote: Reports for this site go out through the email service set up on {host}.
assistant.title: AI Assistant
assistant.about: It answers from {site}'s numbers, which it reads the moment you ask.
assistant.intro: Ask about visitors, sources, pages, goals, or anything else this dashboard shows.
assistant.ask1: How did this period compare with the one before?
assistant.ask2: Where are most visitors coming from?
assistant.ask3: Which pages keep people reading longest?
assistant.ask4: Are AI assistants sending visitors here?
assistant.empty: The assistant had nothing to say.
assistant.setupOwner: The assistant needs an AI service to answer with. Add a key for Anthropic, OpenAI, or Gemini, or point it at a model on your own machine.
assistant.setupViewer: The assistant is not set up yet. The owner or an admin can add an AI service in Settings, AI Assistant.
assistant.ownersOnly: Only the owner or an admin can set up the assistant.
assistant.settingsIntro: Choose an AI service and paste an API key from it below. The robot button beside Filter then opens an assistant that answers questions about your stats in plain words.
assistant.privacy: Each question goes to that service with the numbers the assistant reads to answer it. Runlight keeps nothing about individual visitors, so nothing personal is sent. The assistant only reads, through the same tools as the MCP server, so it can never change anything.
assistant.notEncryptedTitle: Your key will be stored unencrypted
assistant.notEncrypted: This Runlight has no RUNLIGHT_SECRET, so the key is kept in its database exactly as you type it. Set RUNLIGHT_SECRET or RUNLIGHT_TOKEN on the server to keep it encrypted.
assistant.addressHint: Where the service's OpenAI-compatible API lives, ending before /chat/completions.
assistant.addressLocal: Where the model runs. The server running Runlight must be able to reach it.
assistant.modelPlaceholder: The model's name, as the service lists it
assistant.modelHint: Enter the key above, then load the service's models, or type a model's name. A model that can call tools works best.
assistant.removeHint: Removes the service and its key. The robot button then asks an owner to set it up again.
journeys.title: Journeys
journeys.intro: The paths visits take through the site, a page at a time. Click a page to follow only the visits that passed through it.
journeys.none: Try a wider date range to see more visits.
people.emailed: An invite is on its way to {email}. You can also send them this link yourself.
people.noMail: This server has no mail service, so send {email} this link yourself. Set one up in Settings, Email service to send invites by email.
people.mailFailed: The email to {email} did not go out ({error}). Send them this link yourself.
people.linkHint: The link works once, for seven days. Sending again makes a new link and stops this one.
twofa.title: Two-factor sign-in
twofa.off: Off. Turn it on and signing in also asks for a code from an authenticator app on your phone.
twofa.on_one: On. Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app. You have {n} recovery code left.
twofa.on_other: On. Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app. You have {n} recovery codes left.
twofa.scan: Scan this with an authenticator app, such as 1Password, Google Authenticator, or Authy, then enter the six-digit code it shows.
twofa.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
twofa.manual: Or type this key into the app.
twofa.codesIntro: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe. Each one signs you in once if you lose your phone, and they are not shown again.
people.resetTwoFactorHint: Turns off two-factor sign-in for this person, for when they lost their phone and recovery codes
journeys.sampled: These are the paths of the newest {n} visits in these dates.
error.owner_only: Only an owner can change this.
error.domain_invalid: That is not a domain name.

error.link_no_slug: Could not find a free slug. Try again.

error.mail_unset: Set up a mail service first.

error.sample_soon: A sample went out a moment ago. Wait a minute and try again.
error.people_owner: Only the owner or an admin can manage people.
people.demoted: You are a viewer now, so settings are closed and nothing here can be changed. The owner or an admin can change it back.
links.importNoUrl: Nothing was imported because the file has no url column with addresses in it. Use the columns name and url, plus slug and domain when you have them.
app.sessionEnded: You were signed out, which happens when a session runs out or a password changes. {link} and you come back to this view.
links.noneYet: Nobody has made a short link for this site yet.
error.remote_slow: {host} took too long to answer. Try a shorter range.
error.domain_not_public: {domain} is not a public domain name. Use one that browsers anywhere can reach.
error.token_refused: {host} refused the token. Connect it again from the site's settings.
error.mail_failed: The email could not be sent ({detail}).

error.mail_https: The webhook URL must use https.
error.mail_region: That is not an AWS region, like us-east-1.

error.code_wrong: That code is not right. Check the time on your phone and try the next one.
error.twofactor_self: Turn off your own two-factor sign-in under Account.
error.origin_needed: Set this Runlight's own address first (RUNLIGHT_URL on the server, or origin in routes()), so a connected hub can add link domains and email reports.

error.pick_origin: Send the dashboard's origin, such as https://stats.example.com
error.pick_hub: This hub's address is not the one it connected from. Connect the site again from here.
assistant.viewerDaily: Questions each viewer can ask a day
assistant.viewerDailyHint: Every question is paid for with your AI key. Viewers are the people you invite under People who can read stats but change nothing, and each of them can ask this many a day. Set 0 to keep the assistant for owners. Share links never get the assistant.
error.assistant_soon: You have asked a lot in a short time. Wait a little and ask again.
error.assistant_daily: Viewers can ask {limit} questions a day. Ask again tomorrow.
error.assistant_limit: Use a whole number from 0 to 1,000.
error.token_unset: Set RUNLIGHT_TOKEN, or pass token or authorize to routes(). Without one, Runlight only runs open when NODE_ENV is development.
error.unauthorized: Sign in or send a token to see this.

error.unknown_share: That share link no longer exists.
error.token_site: A token that changes settings is for one site. Pick the site.
error.sites_in_code: Sites are set in code here, so they are changed there.

error.site_remote: This site is counted by its own Runlight. Connect it again from its settings to change it from here.

error.check_not_public: it is not a public domain name

empty.pages.title: Your top pages will show up here
empty.pages.hint: Every page people open is listed, with how long they stay on it.
empty.sources.title: Your traffic sources will show up here
empty.sources.hint: The searches and sites that send people your way are listed by name.
empty.locations.title: Your visitors’ locations will show up here
empty.locations.hint: See which countries and cities people visit from.
empty.rhythm.title: Your busiest times will show up here
empty.rhythm.hint: Each hour of the week fills in as visits come in.
